scenes.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: one landscape inline picture for chapter 4 of a graded Japanese reader.
Input images: Image 1 is the approved Kasa Jizō inline style reference only. Image 2 is the shared series cover, for Haru's character identity and palette only.
Primary request: Show Haru and her grandmother in the quiet back room beside an old wooden pillar, as the grandmother recognizes the height marks of the brother she had forgotten.
Scene/backdrop: A modest back room in an old Japanese home. One thick, dark wooden pillar stands clearly in view, with two simple columns of small horizontal child-height marks carved or drawn into it; one column stops lower than the other. Keep the rest of the room spare and quiet.
Subject: Haru, a young girl with long dark hair and muted teal clothes, stands beside her elderly grandmother. The grandmother has a soft grey hair bun and simple muted plum and sage clothing; she gently rests one hand on the pillar and looks moved, as though a long-lost memory has returned. Haru watches her with quiet attention.
Style/medium: Follow Image 1's inline treatment: broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours, minimal texture, a few purposeful folds and shadows, and quiet simplified backgrounds. Use Image 2 only for Haru's character identity and palette, not its detailed cover rendering.
Composition/framing: Wide landscape near 12:7, with the marked pillar as the focal form and the two figures clearly readable beside it; simple two or three depth layers.
Lighting/mood: Soft natural daylight, intimate, reflective and tender.
Color palette: Muted teal, sage, warm ivory, plum, soft ochre and dark warm wood.
Constraints: Depict the moment from paragraph 5. The pillar may have plain marks only: no legible names, numbers, letters, writing, captions, text, border, watermark or decorative frame. No photographs or later-story scenes.

Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: one landscape inline story painting for chapter 4, “Marks on the Pillar,” in a graded Japanese reader.
Input images: Images 1–3 are the approved Kasa Jizō inline paintings and define only the simpler inline treatment: broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours, minimal texture and quiet backgrounds. Image 4 is the shared series cover, for Haru’s character identity and palette only. Image 5 is the existing painting for this chapter and guides Haru’s appearance and colours only; do not copy its composition or the cover’s detailed rendering.
Primary request: depict paragraph 0: the next morning, Haru checks the faded reminder on her left hand and goes over it again with a pen.
Scene/backdrop: a quiet morning in a modest Japanese home, with Haru seated on a simple futon in a sparse tatami room. A shoji window lets in soft pale daylight; use only a few broad shapes and no busy room details.
Subject: Haru is a young girl with long dark hair tied back, wearing her familiar muted teal clothes. She sits up and looks closely at her open left palm, holding a simple pen in her right hand as she carefully darkens a few tiny, pale, non-legible marks on her skin. The hand gesture and her concerned, thoughtful face are the focal points. Keep both hands natural and clearly formed.
Style/medium: children’s picture-book gouache in the approved Kasa Jizō inline treatment: broad mostly smooth colour shapes, gentle contours, minimal surface texture, a few purposeful folds and shadows, and a quiet simplified background. Much simpler than any cover.
Composition/framing: wide landscape near 12:7, medium close view of Haru seated, with her face, left palm and pen large and readable; two or three calm depth layers and breathing room.
Lighting/mood: soft early-morning light, intimate and reflective, with a small note of unease but never frightening.
Color palette: warm ivory, muted teal, sage, soft ochre, simple natural wood and a little blue-grey.
Constraints: show no other person. No readable letters, numbers, words or symbols on the hand, pen, room, or elsewhere; only faint abstract marks. No text, captions, lettering, border, watermark or decorative frame. No later-story clues or supernatural effects.

Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: one quiet landscape inline story painting for chapter 4, “Marks on the Pillar,” in a graded Japanese reader.
Input images: Images 1–3 are the approved Kasa Jizō inline paintings and define only the simpler treatment: broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours, minimal texture and quiet backgrounds. Image 4 guides Haru’s character identity and palette only. Image 5 is the existing painting for this chapter and guides Haru’s appearance and colours only; do not copy its composition or cover-like detail.
Primary request: depict paragraph 8: Haru carefully peels an old photograph from the album, hoping to help the boy whose shadow appears in the picture.
Scene/backdrop: a simple old Japanese home with a low wooden table and an open clothbound photo album. Keep the room quiet, uncluttered and secondary.
Subject: Haru, a young girl with long dark hair tied back and a muted teal outfit, uses both hands to lift the corner of a small black-and-white photograph from one album page. Make the careful peeling action clear. The old photograph itself is visible and shows a little girl on stone shrine steps; beside her is the distinct shadow of a boy wearing a wide-brimmed straw hat, but no boy is physically present in the photo. Haru’s face is thoughtful and intent.
Style/medium: children’s picture-book gouache in the approved Kasa Jizō inline treatment: broad smooth colour shapes, gentle contours, minimal surface texture, a few purposeful folds and shadows, and a quiet simplified background. Much simpler than a cover.
Composition/framing: wide landscape near 12:7, medium view with Haru’s face, both hands and the lifted photograph large and readable. The photograph is a modest focal detail, not a complex picture-within-picture; use only a few broad shapes.
Lighting/mood: soft overcast afternoon light, careful and quietly hopeful, never frightening.
Color palette: warm ivory, muted teal, soft wood brown, sage and restrained blue-grey; keep the photograph softly monochrome.
Constraints: depict only this moment from paragraph 8. No grandmother or Sora. The boy appears only as a shadow inside the photograph. No other supernatural effects, readable writing, names, numbers, text, captions, lettering, border, watermark or decorative frame.
